terms.latin: alumnus, alumnī m.; alumna, alumnae f.
terms.gloss: a child nursed or brought up by someone, as that person’s nursling
evidence: Plaut. Merc. 809: Erus atque alumnus tuos sum.
Plaut. Cist. 762: nostra haec alumna est
terms.comment: From alō, rear. Most frequent in the poets (Lewis & Short). The sense “former pupil” is modern.

phrases.latin: Erus atque alumnus tuos sum. — Salvē, alumne mī.
phrases.english: I am your master, and the child you nursed. — Hello, my nursling.
